title: Call inspector sandbox — live inference debugger ideas
summary: Collection of ideas for a lightweight interactive inspector for individual LLM calls — step-through token generation, latency/cost breakdown, KV view, and replay-and-edit flow. Goal: let backend+frontend devs debug model outputs without duplicating infra or leaking customer data.
body:
Goal / quick pitch:

Make it trivial for engineers to understand why a single model response looked the way it did. Right now you have logs (opaque), traces (latency only), and reproductions (annoying). Call Inspector = an in-browser / CLI inspector that attaches to a request ID and exposes: token-by-token trace, prefix/kv snapshot, policy fallbacks, batching/queue wait, cost estimate, and ability to replay with small edits (temperature, prompt patch).

Key capabilities (brainstorm):
- Attach by request-id or session-id. Minimal privacy mode: redact user PII unless dev opts in.
- Token timeline: streaming tokens with timestamps, source (model/tokenizer/hallucination heuristics), confidence-ish proxy (logprobs if available).
- KV cache inspector: show kv cache keys/contents for recent layers (summary, not full tensors) — e.g., token keys, attention cache sizes, whether cache hit used for prefix.
- Model routing info: which variant served (quantized fallback vs full), what triggered fallback (quota, cold start, error).
- Cost & latency breakdown: queue time, batch wait, compute, token emission; token-level cost estimate.
- Replay & fork: clone the exact call (seed/temperature/kwargs), allow line-edit to prompt or change params, re-run in sandbox (isolated, no real user send). Capture diffs and mark as 'reproducible' or 'non-deterministic'.
- Snapshot compare: compare two runs token-by-token, diff with color-coded insert/delete/replace.
- Save as reproduction: store minimal artifact (prompt + rand-seed + model-version + snapshot of relevant cache pointers) for bug reports.
- Annotations: let devs pin notes at token indices, attach Jira/Slack links.

User stories (first-pass):
- As an FE engineer, I want to see why the assistant returned an extra sentence after a prompt edit, so I can fix the prompt template.
- As an infra engineer, I want to know whether a slow tail was due to batching or GPU scheduling so I can tweak autoscaling.
- As a support engineer, I want to save a reproducible artifact to attach to a customer's ticket without exposing PII.
- As an ML engineer, I want to compare outputs across two quantization profiles for the same prompt to validate degradations.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Attach to a request-id and render token timeline + overall latency/cost breakdown in the Console.
- Replay flow that reproduces with same seed/params for deterministic models (documented behavior for non-deterministic).
- Basic KV cache summary (counts + per-layer size) without exposing raw embeddings.
- Redaction toggle and clear UX copy on privacy risk.

Surface / API design notes:
- New API: GET /inspector/{request_id} -> metadata + events stream (text tokens, timestamps, events like fallback).
- POST /inspector/replay -> create ephemeral replay job with override params, returns ephemeral replay-id and logs.
- Attach front-end: Console -> Devtools area -> Inspector pane; lightweight CLI: ri inspect <request-id> --replay
- Storage: store only derived metadata for 7 days by default; reproductions (explicit saves) kept per team policy.

Telemetry needed:
- How often inspectors are opened (gauge), replay attempts, successful reproductions, common param overrides (temp changes), redact-toggle usage.
- Sampling policy: only sample for paid orgs / internal devs by default. PII/consent flags mandatory.

Privacy & security considerations:
- By default, redact input text (hash & token counts only). Devs must enable a "show raw input" with explicit warning and org-level admin opt-in.
- Saved reproductions should strip UUIDs and replace email-like tokens unless saved by an admin.
- Access controls: only team members on the request owner's org or internal SRE can open inspector. Integrate with Console RBAC.

Rough UI sketch (text):
- Left column: request metadata (model, region, request-id, time, user-id masked), quick actions (replay, save, link to ticket).
- Middle: token timeline (scrollable) with per-token timestamp, emission latency, optional show-logprobs toggle. Click token -> open small pane showing nearby prompt + heuristics.
- Right: sidepanel tabs: KV summary, cost & latency waterfall, model routing, saved reproductions.
- Top: replay bar (temperature, top_p, max_tokens override) + Run button -> creates ephemeral replay and streams results into a new timeline.

Perf cost estimates / operational notes:
- Inspector should not keep full tensors for privacy and cost. For KV we store counts + small hashed summaries and scalar sizes.
- Replay jobs should be rate-limited and run on lower-priority pool to avoid affecting production SLOs. Maybe spawn as Dedicated-mini or sandbox queue.

Phased rollout / experiment ideas:
- Phase 0: internal-only alpha for DX and SRE with full raw data access. Collect feedback.
- Phase 1: Console feature (read-only) with redaction default for early adopter orgs. Measure time-to-debug uplift via telemetry.
- Phase 2: public opt-in with saved reproductions and Jira/Slack integration.
- Experiment: A/B test whether redaction default increases adoption vs trust concerns.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to represent KV cache without exposing embeddings? (ideas: minhash sketches, quantized checksums, token-wise provenance summary).
- Reproducibility guarantees for models with non-deterministic ops — should we expose seed/machine-id? probably not. Document expected nondeterminism.
- Cost policy: charge replay token usage to a separate credits pool? free for internal? Need billing design.
- UX: do we show logprobs by default? Might leak model internals. Add admin toggle.

Notes-to-self / quick tasks:
- Talk to infra about a sandbox queue for replay jobs (SLA, priority). /ptr @Kai
- Draft privacy copy and admin opt-in flows; run by legal (Kiera?).
- Prototype token timeline as React component using existing streaming APIs (look at console chat stream components).
- Add small telemetry plan in ENG-4821 and link to growth metrics (time to resolve tickets).

Random heuristics & ideas to capture:
- Inline "why this token" helper: combine logprob dips + prompt boundary to show likely trigger.
- Auto-detect likely hallucination: compare entity tokens vs knowledge base hits (if integrated). Flag with caution ribbon.
- Lightweight snapshot diff encoding (like patch) so saved reproductions are small and shareable.

End of pad. This is messy — meant to be a working parking lot. Will tidy into a one-pager if we decide to scope MVP.
